rationale: The Stage 1 evaluation for scope MULTIBRAND-OPERATOR-01 results in INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE because zero evidence records in the audited dataset are verified as IN_SCOPE for the target buyer profile. While 41 practitioner records describe social media content production and multi-client workflows (with 38 verified records across 35 independent entities), none explicitly substantiate all five operational scope criteria: an external service provider, multiple unrelated client brands, recurring static content/revision work, owner-operator hands-on involvement, and confirmed SMB clientele. In strict adherence to workspace validation rules (never invent a fact, UNKNOWN is a valid result, do not fabricate SMB focus or buyer authority), these practitioner records remain UNKNOWN scope. Consequently, Gates G1 through G5 have an independent in-scope count of 0 and cannot pass. Furthermore, because no in-scope records exist to substantiate decisive contradictions, Gates G1 through G5 cannot fail. Gate G6 (No killer substitute) is evaluated as UNKNOWN because serious incumbents (Canva Pro/Business, Planable, Adobe Express) and stitched manual workflows demonstrate high observed sufficiency and low friction in practice, while key operational gaps (detached Bulk Create output, lack of dynamic revision propagation, and version desynchronization) remain unresolved threats rather than proven monopolies or disqualifying substitutes. With six gates UNKNOWN and zero gates FAIL, the canonical decision is INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE, and Stage 2 prospect mining or interviews are not authorized.
scope_integrity_notes: Target scope MULTIBRAND-OPERATOR-01 requires five concurrent criteria: external service provider (not in-house), multiple unrelated client brands, recurring static content/revision work, owner-operator hands-on production or revision role, and confirmed SMB clientele.
Zero records in the dataset meet all five criteria with verified primary evidence; by_scope.IN_SCOPE contains 0 records and 0 verified independence keys.

41 practitioner records remain in UNKNOWN scope because source texts do not explicitly verify hands-on ownership and SMB client focus; per validation rules, missing attributes cannot be inferred or upgraded.

30 records are OUT_OF_SCOPE: 28 software vendor documentation/pricing records (Canva, Adobe, Planable, Kontentino, SocialPilot, Buffer, Predis.ai, Ocoya, Abyssale, Bannerbear, PostFlow, Juicer) and 2 explicitly excluded single-brand practitioners (mb-wtp-005 single-brand business owner, mb-pain-017 in-house marketing employee).
No pooling of solo freelancer signals and agency signals is permitted to manufacture a passing gate; both sub-segments remain unattributed to confirmed in-scope status.

candidate_scope_assessments.reason: Single-brand in-house corporate or nonprofit marketing teams managing internal social channels with multi-tiered compliance review. Excluded from MULTIBRAND-OPERATOR-01 due to single-brand context and absence of multi-client tenant switching.

Mid-to-large digital agencies (50+ employees) with specialized departmental roles (dedicated copywriters, art directors, account managers), formal SSO/security procurement, and complex billing infrastructure. Excluded from owner-led SMB provider focus.

G6.threshold_or_rule: No evidenced sufficient low-friction substitute; material unresolved threats stay UNKNOWN.

high_impact_excluded.reason: Canva Pro ($18/mo) and Business ($25/user/mo) provide cheap multi-brand kits and templates; observed as strong substitute with high adoption, but bulk revision propagation and version sync remain unresolved.
Canva Bulk Create generates up to 300 designs from CSV; output is detached, leaving revision propagation unresolved.
Planable workspaces ($33-$59/workspace/mo) provide multi-client approval routing with unlimited guest review; lacks native graphic authoring, leaving composite stack friction unresolved.

Freelance SMM creates weekly batches across multiple clients in a few hours using Canva templates; demonstrates high observed sufficiency of manual template workflows, but client scale limits remain unverified.
Agency marketer observed that automated content generation collapsed client engagement; shows severe automation backlash, challenging standalone AI production tools.
Agency operator reports internal production runs smoothly in Trello, while the real bottleneck is client asset/approval latency; challenges the value proposition of drafting speed.

Agency team uses a single shared Canva document formatted as mock posts for real-time client collaboration; demonstrates that live web links bypass file export friction, threatening flat-pack handoffs.
Adobe Express Teams ($6.49/seat/mo) syncs CC Libraries across brands; layout-level revision propagation across generated variants remains unresolved.
Predis.ai ($24-$212/mo) generates brief-to-post batches with brand colors; outputs flat raster images with no dynamic template propagation and high editing friction.
Abyssale ($36/seat/mo) provides dynamic template revision propagation; tailored for ad banners rather than organic social workflows and client review UX.

material_unknowns: Whether the existing composite stack (Canva for design + Planable for client approval + Trello for workflow) is observed as sufficient by owner-operators despite lack of unified integration

Whether the low pricing ceiling established by Canva ($18-$25/mo) and Planable ($39-$59/workspace) allows viable unit economics for a standalone multi-brand engine
